clue.text: Clean breaks round bone left as result of car crash?

indicators.note: the word for clean splits open to go around the other pieces, so it breaks round them

parts.note: to clean is to wash
the hip is a bone

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up broken bones after a road accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A neck injury from a sudden jolt, typical of rear-end collisions, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Rider perhaps gets a little beer down

parts.note: a half is a half pint of beer
blue means sad, down

explanation.surface: A horseman drinks a small beer and feels low.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a half blue is awarded for a minor sport, so a rider in the equestrian team is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxbridge sporting award for lesser sports, which a university rider might win.

clue.text: Deliriously happy person offering coins for a ring here

indicators.note: in a frenzied state, so the letters are tumbled

parts.note: one means a person

explanation.surface: An ecstatic suitor offers money in exchange for a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a wedding band; it is a telephone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A public telephone takes coins so you can make a call, a ring.

clue.text: Offered by law a year off

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A year's leave granted by statute.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent, as in a player who is off or out of the office.

clue.text: Regularly heal: lucky wound is undisturbed

indicators.note: every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A lucky wound heals steadily and is left alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and peaceful, as in halcyon days.

clue.text: Lucky art of making valuable contacts

definitions.text: Lucky art of making valuable contacts

parts.words: Lucky art of making valuable contacts
parts.note: read as the myth of a king whose every touch turned things to gold, and the knack of networking profitably

explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial ability to make money from everything one touches, from the legend of King Midas.

clue.text: Succeeded getting free — that's to save one's skin

parts.note: to unblock is to free from obstruction

explanation.surface: Escaping is a way of saving your own skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save one's skin' suggests escape; literally it is sunscreen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream that protects skin from the sun's rays.

clue.text: Time is against us

definitions.meaning: in old slang, how goes ... means what time is it

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls time the foe, and the opposing side is the foe in battle.

clue.text: A dog grabbed foreign character? That's not on

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the female dog takes hold of the Greek letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a bitch is a female dog
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dog seizes a stranger, which is hardly acceptable behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is excessive or unreasonable is the same idiom as saying it is not on.

clue.text: Most boys love to cooperate

parts.note: read as the game most boys enjoy, an invitation to throw a ball about; also the idiom for working together

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for agreeing to work along with others comes from joining in a ball game.

clue.text: A club he's trashed, that one is celebrating in

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters H, E, S as printed

explanation.surface: A nightclub wrecked by a man who was celebrating in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrating' points at a party, but the celebrant here is a priest saying Mass, and this vestment is what he wears.
explanation.definitionFit: The sleeveless outer vestment worn by the priest who celebrates the Eucharist.

clue.text: Following claret with second, stronger wine is a deadly pursuit

parts.note: claret is old slang for blood, from its colour
port is a fortified wine, stronger than table wine

explanation.surface: A connoisseur moves from claret to a fortified wine, a dangerous hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret looks like the wine it is beside, but here it is boxing slang for blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting activity in which animals are killed for entertainment.

clue.text: Scrambled equaliser, first for Manchester City

indicators.note: the letters are scrambled into a new order
the opening letter of the word Manchester is taken

explanation.surface: A frantic late goal for Manchester City.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester City suggests football, but City is the financial district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The City of London's financial district is nicknamed after its area of about one square mile.

clue.text: Look intently in small opening

definitions.meaning: to study something closely, as over a book
a tiny hole in the skin

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to read or study with close attention; the noun is a minute skin orifice.

clue.text: With herb banks, smooth stream, perhaps

indicators.note: the herb lies on either side of the other piece, like banks around a river

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb
even means smooth, level

explanation.surface: A gentle stream flowing between herb-covered banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The river picture misleads: the stream is an income stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is often described as a stream, so a revenue stream is one example.

clue.text: Fight and plunder carrier

parts.note: a ruck is a brawl
to sack is to plunder

explanation.surface: Fighting and looting by a delivery firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpack is a bag for carrying things.

clue.text: Unexplained changes in veto a good sign

annotationWithheld.why: Unexplained changes in veto a good sign: A G ARIES from 'a good sign' leaves V for 'in veto' with no reading; likely OCR garble and the down clues are not on the scan
annotationWithheld.clue: Unexplained changes in veto a good sign

clue.text: Plan finally to partition country found in old locker

indicators.note: the single letter splits the country in two

parts.note: Turkey is a country

indicators.note: the last letter of the word plan is taken

explanation.surface: A scheme to divide a nation discovered in an ancient strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailer of old kept the keys and locked up prisoners.

clue.text: Countryman using logic has name for river

indicators.note: the logical word takes in a replacement letter
one letter stands in for another

parts.note: rational means using logic

explanation.surface: A logical man from the country names a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a particular nation, a fellow countryman.

clue.text: A tangled mop, some sheep — otherwise short coats

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps around the sheep word
the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: else means otherwise
a flock is a group of sheep

explanation.surface: Shaggy sheep with short fleeces.
explanation.definitionFit: Matted, tangled locks of hair, once blamed on elves.

clue.text: Reticent with escort

definitions.meaning: cautious, careful about what is said

explanation.definitionFit: Means cautious in speech, and also protected by a minder.

clue.text: Like bars giving little away

definitions.meaning: jocularly, having the look of a cage

explanation.definitionFit: Means wary and uncommunicative, and jokingly cage-like with bars.

clue.text: In furs, fought violently — the result?

definitions.text: In furs, fought violently — the result?

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about violently into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: People in fur coats came to blows, with predictable consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent, rowdy behaviour is what a brawl produces.

clue.text: First to spurn powdered milk!

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word spurn is taken

parts.note: creamer is a powdered milk substitute for coffee

explanation.surface: An exclamation at being the first to refuse powdered milk.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark is the definition: printers call it a screamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers' and journalists' slang for an exclamation mark.

clue.text: Article doctor's put into book

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
MO, medical officer, is a doctor, with 's

explanation.surface: A physician's article is published in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Old Testament named after a prophet.

clue.text: Make taxi drop last one off in the country

parts.note: to do is to make

indicators.note: the final letter of the cab word is dropped

parts.note: a minicab is a taxi booked by phone

explanation.surface: A cab driver lets the last passenger out in some country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island nation in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: Hellenic woven cloth

indicators.note: woven threads are interlaced, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fabric woven in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft tufted velvety fabric, a type of cloth.

clue.text: Announce daughter's about to arrive?

parts.note: D for daughter, with 's standing for is
something close is near at hand

explanation.surface: Telling everyone a daughter's baby is due soon.
explanation.definitionFit: To make known or reveal is a synonym for announcing.
